extracted.intended_audience: readers seeking recommendations of books by queer writers of color (general readers, book buyers, book-club members)
extracted.subtask_short: curated queer writers of color list
extracted.subtask_description: A publisher-curated list of recommended books by queer writers of color, highlighting notable works across fiction, memoir, poetry, and essays with brief descriptive blurbs and buying links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unflinching honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are told with unflinching honesty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intro framing: recommended books are noted for candid, uncompromising portrayals of experience. Examples from the list include works described as 'unflinching' in their exploration of identity and lived experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powerful prose / stylistic strength
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selections emphasize strong, affecting writing—lyrical or sharply observed language that carries the emotional weight of the story. Examples: Ocean Vuong (The Emperor of Gladness) and Jacqueline Woodson (Red at the Bone) called out for lyrical eloquence and powerful storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling, lovable characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters that you will absolutely fall in love with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books are chosen for well-drawn, emotionally engaging characters whose inner lives and relationships drive the books—e.g., Leila Mottley's teenage mothers, the narrators of Memorial and Skye Falling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beloved / re-readable works (lasting impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novels are read, reread, and cherished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selections are framed as enduring works that reward multiple readings and have lasting resonance; editorial language frames many titles as 'celebrated' or 'essential'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploration of chosen family, love, and relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on chosen family, love, and the forms relationships take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many blurbs highlight themes of chosen family and intimate bonds (e.g., Ocean Vuong's bighearted novel about chosen family; Memorial's exploration of family in strange forms; Queer Love in Color's photographic celebration of relationships).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersectional identity and lived experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention to the intersections of race, gender, sexuality, class, disability, and migration in characters' lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list privileges works that center intersecting identities—explicit phrases include 'intersections of queer and POC identities', and blurbs call out explorations of race, gender, immigration, and disability (e.g., Shayla Lawson's essays; Paul Tran's poetry investigating intergenerational trauma and sexual violence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyrical / poetic language and voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Lyrical, poetic, or highly crafted language is a hallmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several entries are praised for lyricism ('lyrical eloquence', 'incisive, unflinching, and lyrical') and include poets or poet-novelists (e.g., Paul Tran, Ocean Vuong, Jacqueline Woodson).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional range and resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Books convey a wide emotional register—tenderness, heartbreak, hope, longing, humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blurbs emphasize emotional effects: 'heartrending', 'tenderly examines', 'joys and entanglements', 'funny and profound'. Works are selected for their capacity to move readers across affective tones (e.g., The Girls Who Grew Big; Quietly Hostile; Martyr!).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provocative thematic inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Poses provocative questions about family, freedom, identity, and survival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selections engage difficult, provocative themes—e.g., Necessary Fiction 'poses these provocative questions' about family and freedom; books that interrogate societal constraints and personal survival are foregrounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre-blending and formal experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of hybrid forms (memoir-in-essays, photographic collections, poetry, essays, experimental fiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list includes works that cross or blend genres (Alligator Tears as 'memoir-in-essays', Queer Love in Color as a photographic collection, collections of essays/poetry), signaling value placed on formal innovation and multiplicity of modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor and comic voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective use of humor, dark comedy, or comic timing alongside serious themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries cite 'darkly comic', 'hilarious', and 'laugh-out-loud moments' as positive qualities (e.g., Alligator Tears, Quietly Hostile), indicating that humor that illuminates experience is a selection criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and political critique / engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement with social issues (racism, sexism, homophobia, imperialism, class) and critique of structures of power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many blurbs highlight books that take on systemic issues explicitly ('takes on sexism, racism, ageism, homophobia, and class'; 'U.S. imperialism'; 'powerfully disrupts constraints of race, gender, and disability'), showing an editorial preference for politically engaged writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and distinctive voice
rubrics_metrics.description: A singular, original voice or perspective—groundbreaking or wholly original work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several blurbs praise works as 'wholly original', 'a singular and stunning collection', or 'groundbreaking' (e.g., Martyr!, The Black Period, Magical/Realism), indicating originality as a key criterion.
